newsitem.title: INDIA: Depression off south Indian coast, heavy rain seen.
newsitem.headline: Depression off south Indian coast, heavy rain seen.

text.p: Indian meteorological authorities said on Friday a depression had formed in the Bay of Bengal off the southern coast and was likely to intensify later, accompanied by heavy rain.

The depression lay 550 km east of the southern Indian city of Madras early on Thursday and was likely to intensify further and move in a north-north westerly direction, the Indian Meteorological Dept in New Delhi said in a statement.
Heavy rainfall was expected in the coastal areas of the south Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, it said.
Authorities warned fishermen not to go out to sea off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and the neighbouring state of Orissa.

Earlier this month, the Andhra Pradesh coast was devastated by a cyclonic storm causing 971 deaths. A further 925 were missing, according to official figures. More than 177,000 people had to be evacuated from areas inundated by heavy rains.
The damage to property then was estimated to be more than 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion), officials said.
